key_insight: A low-density, anisotropic Fourier-space triadic model still reproduces the core 2D turbulence double-cascade and Richardson superdiffusion, showing that sparse resonant interactions can preserve key turbulent physics.
engineering_relevance: This suggests reduced-order turbulence models can lower computational cost while retaining cascade and dispersion behavior relevant to mixing, transport, and flow prediction.
method: Sampled active triads on an ordered pseudo-logarithmic or disordered Fourier mesh
Controlled spectral anisotropy through angular sampling and triadic density
Evaluated inverse cascade and particle-pair dispersion in Eulerian and Lagrangian frames
evidence_signal: Across all configurations, the abstract reports a robust $k^{-5/3}$ inverse cascade, a $k^{-3}$ direct cascade, and pair dispersion scaling as $\ell^2(t)\sim t^3$ before crossing to Brownian $\ell^2(t)\sim t$ at long times.
watch_item: The reduced anisotropic mesh changes vorticity organization and flux efficiency, so amplitude and transport details may be model-dependent even when scaling laws are preserved.
paper_title: Exploring 2D turbulent properties in anisotropic and disordered Fourier space: Insights into inverse cascades and universal superdiffusion from randomly sampled triadic interaction
